slides.title: Two questions at the counter
slides.text: When you collect a package, Pim checks two different things. Authentication proves it is really you. Authorization checks the list to see if this package is yours to open.

slides.title: Know, have, are
slides.text: Sign-in checks come in three kinds. Two different kinds protect you far better than two of the same kind.
steps: code sent to a phone: something you have
slides.alt: The Pro mailbox key builder: a passphrase made of chosen words, different from every other account key.

focus.cue: Something you know: the passphrase you build here
Words nobody could guess about you

slides.title: Passkeys, honestly
slides.text: A passkey lives on your device, which proves it is you without sharing a copyable secret. A fake page cannot trick you into handing it over, because there is nothing to hand over.

slides.title: Shared screens, separate doors
slides.text: On a shared tablet or class account, profiles and permissions matter. Your profile keeps your work, messages and settings separate from everyone else who uses the same screen.
slides.alt: A tablet holds messages and pictures. Signing out on a shared computer: does the habit protect it, or is it risky?

focus.cue: Signing out on a shared computer: the habit that separates you
Protects it, or risky? Profiles keep people apart

a key kept on your device that proves it is you

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Trick Inbox at Prize Letters and sort all 7 messages. When a letter fishes for your mailbox key, name the check that would still stop a thief: something you have, or something you are.
slides.alt: A letter from the Post Office Team says your mailbox will close unless you send your mailbox key today.
